x.note: queryIds rotate ~2-4 weeks; Bookmarks has its own. features blob is inherited via MAIN-world interception, never hardcoded.

xTimeline.note: The canary's OWN X capture, separate from the hand-composed x-bookmarks.json the unit tests pin against (see scripts/drift-check.js FIXTURE.x). Captured live 2026-08-13 from a real bookmarks timeline: 3 tweets (1 video, 1 four-photo, 1 text-only) + Top/Bottom cursors, parsing to tweetCount=3 mediaItems=7. Sanitized by a key-INDEPENDENT value sweep (profile/media/video/t.co urls, every >=15-digit snowflake, every *_count, view counts, handles, names, bios, texts, cursors, node ids), then audited by checking every leaf string of the original against the output — what survives is schema constants plus video bitrates, which are load-bearing (the mapper picks the highest-bitrate MP4).

xThread.queryIdSource: scraped from abs.twimg.com/responsive-web/**/*.js at sweep time (never hardcoded — TweetDetail has its own id and it rotates with the rest)
xThread.entryShapes: focal tweet as a bare TimelineTimelineItem; continuations nested inside a conversationthread MODULE — collectConversationTweets walks generically so either can move alone
xThread.note: Live-validated 2026-08-13 against a real 29-tweet conversation: a 5-tweet self-thread, 12 author-replies-to-commenters, 13 authors. The capture ALSO caught a live break — X no longer ships api.*.js and the operation->queryId table now lives in main.*.js, so the old api-only bundle match found nothing and expansion was silently off. features={} was accepted with no repair round on this date. Fixture is sanitized: handles, display names, bios, ids, node ids, media/profile/t.co urls and post text are all synthetic; keys, nesting and reply structure are verbatim.

pinterest.note: Re-verified live 2026-08-14. X-APP-VERSION DRIFTS INTRADAY, not on a release cadence: 194583e and be501f2 were observed FOUR HOURS APART on the same day (and 1df0da9 42 days before). Treat the value here as a sample, never a constant — it is scraped at runtime and never sent from here. The SOLE 403 gatekeeper on /resource/ is still x-pinterest-pws-handler (019 T10, reconfirmed): omit it -> 403, send it -> 200. NEW: the value is presence-checked, NOT route-matched — BoardsResource returned 200 for BOTH 'www/[username].js' and 'www/[username]/[slug].js', so the boards path is no longer blocked on discovering its own handler. Bracketed segments stay literal (never interpolated). Capture host was REDACTED, normalised to www.pinterest.com in the fixture.

instagram.note: Saved feed is REST api/v1 (not GraphQL), re-verified 2026-08-14 with only x-ig-app-id + credentials:'include'. Fan-out (002 · 1A) keys on per-media `pk`; carousel children under carousel_media[]. Poster at image_versions2.candidates[0], reel video at video_versions[]. PAGINATION NOW FULLY CONFIRMED: page 1 came back more_available:true with next_max_id populated (a 120-char string) — the first non-terminal body ever captured — and feeding it back as ?max_id= returned 200 with 21 further posts. The response cursor field name is no longer inferred from convention. The live page is 1.84MB across 21 posts (108-128 keys per media); the fixture keeps 3 whole posts, one per media_type, byte-for-byte. The composed instagram-saved.json the unit tests use carries 11-13 keys per media, so it could never have answered the canary's question. IG drifts fast — 14d window (vs X/Pinterest 30d).
